source.author: stat
source.text: sic ubi longa vagos lassarunt aequora nautas et signum de puppe datum, posuere parumper bracchia: vix requies, iam vox citat altera remos, ecce iterum immodice venientem eludit et exit sponte ruens mersusque umeris: effunditur ille in caput, assurgentem alio puer improbus ictu perculit eventuque impalluit ipse secundo.
source.text_original: sic ubi longa vagos lassarunt aequora nautas / et signum de puppe datum, posuere parumper / bracchia: vix requies, iam vox citat altera remos, / ecce iterum immodice venientem eludit et exit / sponte ruens mersusque umeris: effunditur ille / in caput, assurgentem alio puer improbus ictu / perculit eventuque impalluit ipse secundo.
source.text_english: So when the long seas have wearied the wandering sailors and the signal has been given from the stern, they lay their arms down for a moment: scarcely a rest, when another cry summons the oars; then, look, he cheats a second coming too far and goes out on his own, falling headlong and submerged to the shoulders; he is flung onto his head, and the naughty boy strikes the rising one with another blow and himself grew pale at the favorable outcome.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: fervere cuncta virum coetu, simul undique cernit delatum nemus et docta resonare bipenni litora; iam pinus gracili dissolvere lamna Thespiaden iungique latus lentoque sequaces molliri videt igne trabes, remisque paratis Pallada velifero quaerentem bracchia malo.
reuse.text_original: fervere cuncta virum coetu, simul undique cernit / delatum nemus et docta resonare bipenni / litora; iam pinus gracili dissolvere lamna / Thespiaden iungique latus lentoque sequaces / molliri videt igne trabes, remisque paratis / Pallada velifero quaerentem bracchia malo.
reuse.text_english: he sees all things seething with a company of men, and at the same time the grove brought in from every side and the shores echoing with the skilled double axe; already the pine is being split into thin planks, the Thespian joined, and the sides fitted together, and the following timbers softened by the slow fire, and Pallas, with the oars prepared, seeking the arms on the sail-bearing mast.
